complexity.notes: The quadratic term comes entirely from pop(0) on a list; draining the frontier with ||collections.deque and popleft|| (or just iterating and building a fresh list) makes the whole traversal O(n). The set2 dedup never fires — every node object in a tree is distinct — so a plain list would do, and the identity-based set is harmless either way. The __iter__ and __next__ methods added to TreeNode are dead code, and redefining the judge-provided class is risky style.
complexity.summary: Iterative BFS that materializes each level as a frontier, collects children into a custom set2 (list plus dedup set) for the next level, and drains the current frontier with pop(0). Popping from the front of a list costs O(width) per node, and the widest level holds about n/2 nodes, so that level alone costs O(n^2).
